brief.reader: Platform or SRE engineer running the Splunk OTel Collector chart on Kubernetes who adds Prometheus scraping for apps that still expose /metrics next to OpenTelemetry
brief.question: We scrape our apps' Prometheus endpoints with the Collector agent on every node, and the app also sends OpenTelemetry metrics. Do our Prometheus counters reach Splunk once per pod, and what is the simplest agent config that guarantees it?

demand.evidence: opentelemetry-collector-contrib issue 48546 '[receiver/prometheus] Implement leader election' (open since May 2026): a DaemonSet with one Prometheus receiver config scrapes the same targets from every instance; commenters weigh the Target Allocator, hashmod sharding and node-scoped pod discovery. OpenTelemetry Collector discussion 9998 'Otel collector deployment with multiple pods result in duplicate metrics' (users still reporting it in June and October 2025). opentelemetry-operator issues 4494 (Target Allocator duplicated targets/metrics, dual stack) and 2251 (double scraping). opentelemetry-collector-contrib issue 12300 (load-balanced Collectors, out-of-order samples). The OpenTelemetry Kubernetes observability blueprint and Bindplane's Kubernetes Prometheus Node source both recommend scraping only pods on the Collector's own node.

brief.decision: How to configure Prometheus scraping on the Splunk OTel Collector agent DaemonSet so each pod is scraped once: a node field selector on the scrape job, or the chart's autodetect.prometheus value
brief.takeaway: On a DaemonSet agent, a Prometheus scrape job with cluster-wide pod discovery runs in every agent, so each pod is scraped once per node (the pods' own scraper records show it). Scoping discovery to the agent's node (one field selector) or using the Splunk OTel Collector chart's autodetect.prometheus (node-scoped through the k8s_observer) scrapes each pod once, and the Prometheus counter in Splunk then matches the pods' own count and OpenTelemetry's pushed count. What the double scraping does in Splunk is stated from the result: if the everywhere runs hold 2 series a target, told apart by host.name or host.id, the counter reaches Splunk once per agent and sums to about twice; if they hold 1, both agents write to one series and the extra scrapes show only in the pods' records. Measured on EKS with two nodes, read back from Splunk per run.
brief.open_question: On EKS with two nodes, one orders pod on each, and the Splunk OTel Collector chart 0.163.1 agent: with a prometheus/orders scrape job using cluster-wide pod discovery, with the same job plus a spec.nodeName field selector, and with autodetect.prometheus=true, two runs each of 20 s at 10 orders a second, how many scraper-and-pod pairs read /metrics, how many series and what total does Splunk hold for the Prometheus counter compared with the pods' own count, which dimensions tell duplicate series apart, and does OpenTelemetry's pushed request count match the pods in every run?

brief.adds: The OpenTelemetry Kubernetes blueprint, Bindplane and Lightstep docs describe node-scoped Prometheus scraping for DaemonSet Collectors, and the Splunk chart documents autodetect.prometheus, but none measures the result in a backend. This lab runs three agent configs on EKS, counts orders in the pods, in Splunk's Prometheus series and in OpenTelemetry's pushed metric side by side, names the dimension that tells duplicate series apart, and records who scraped each pod.
tradeoffs: A node field selector keeps your own scrape job and relabel rules; autodetect needs only the prometheus.io annotations but scrapes every annotated pod on the node
Node-scoped scraping needs an agent on every node that runs scraped pods; a pod on a node without an agent isn't scraped
Cluster-level endpoints such as kube-state-metrics live on one node only, so they suit a single-replica scraper or the Target Allocator rather than this pattern
Pushing OTLP from the app avoids scraping altogether; keeping Prometheus side by side during a move to OpenTelemetry is what this lab covers
One app, two nodes, one load level and a 10 s scrape interval
